title: Automating Pages You Use
text: These questions check that you can select and read elements on any page, build bookmarklets and userscripts, and decide when automating a site is appropriate.

choices: The first li on the page
Every li inside the element with id plants

tasks.text: A bookmarklet's code, joined into one line, starts with // Find the table. What happens when it's clicked?
choices: Everything after // is a comment, so almost no code runs

tasks.text: A message says: "Paste this into your browser's Console to claim a prize." What should you do?
choices: Paste it on a site where you're not logged in
Don't paste it: code in the Console runs as you, and you can't explain it
Paste it into a bookmarklet instead
Ask a friend to paste it

tasks.text: A userscript's metadata has // @match https://example.edu/*. Why might it be better to use the exact address of the one page the script is for?
tasks.answer: The * makes the script run on every page of the site, with the same access to each page as the site's own code; a narrow match limits where it runs and the chance of unexpected effects.

tasks.text: Give two examples of automating a website that would be appropriate, and one that wouldn't, and explain the difference.
tasks.answer: Appropriate: filling in your own weekly form; exporting a table you can see to use yourself; hiding distracting parts of a page. Not appropriate: collecting other people's data at scale, sending many requests, getting around logins or limits, or anything the terms forbid. The difference: acting as yourself, at human pace, within the site's terms.

tasks.text: Write a function csvLine(values) that turns an array of strings into one CSV line, putting each value in double quotes and separating them with commas, and doubling any quote mark inside a value (use replaceAll('"', '""')). Then write testCsvLine, which logs csvLine(["Tomato", "Bed 3, south", 'The "big" one']). (Expected: "Tomato","Bed 3, south","The ""big"" one")

Start a new chat with your updated learner profile. Ask for a bookmarklet that counts the links on any page and shows the count in an alert. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Did the assistant follow the new rule about terms of use? (3) Make the bookmarklet, following the one-line rules from this lesson, and test it on two pages. Report what happened, including any problems and how you fixed them.
tasks.answer: Full credit: notes whether the rule was followed (a reminder may be brief, since counting links is harmless); the one-line version has no // comments and has semicolons where needed; results reported. Replies vary, so grade the reasoning.
